headline: Approved off-site improvement agreement with Procopio for Thornton Hill and Rosecrans Drive, 4-1, and a tentative IAFF Local 3160 contract.
summary: Staff previewed preliminary FY 28 budgets, including $547,623 for the Town Manager's department and $1,227,534 for IT. A consultant reported an average road score of 70 out of 100 across 372.36 lane miles. Residents raised impact fees and the fire chief's pay, and a councilor raised concerns about a legal invoice over $125,000.
decisions: Accepted the resignation of Meridel Allen from the Senior Resources Committee, 5-0.
Approved the tentative contract with IAFF Local 3160 for July 1, 2027 through June 30, 2030, subject to voter approval of cost items, 5-0.
Scheduled a public hearing for November 30, 2026 at 7 p.m. on the Water Special Assessment District, 5-0.
Authorized the Acting Town Manager to sign the Off-Site Improvements Agreement with PE Realty Partners (Procopio), 4-1.
Approved the consent agenda items, including the 2026-11-02 Sewer Warrant, 5-0.
Agreed by consensus to add using UFB to offset the tax rate to the November 16 agenda.

decision_evidence.quote: Councilor Bouchard moved that the Londonderry Town Council hereby accepts the resignation of Meridel Allen from the Senior Resources Committee. Seconded by Vice Chair Faber. Motion carried 5-0-0. Chair votes in the affirmative.

Councilor Bouchard moved that the Londonderry Town Council hereby approve the tentative successor collective bargaining agreement between the Town and IAFF Local 3160 for July 1, 2027 through June 30, 2030, subject to voter approval of applicable cost items and other required approvals. Seconded by Councilor Combes. Motion carried 5-0-0. Chair votes in the affirmative.

Vice Chair Faber moved that the Londonderry Town Council hereby schedules a public hearing on November 30, 2026 at 7 p.m. in the Moose Hill Chambers of the Londonderry Town Hall on the proposed Water Special Assessment District. Seconded by Councilor Paul. Motion carried 5-0-0. Chair votes in the affirmative.

Councilor Combes moved that the Londonderry Town Council hereby authorizes the Acting Town Manager to enter into the Off-Site Improvements Agreement and to take all actions necessary to effectuate the agreement. Seconded by Vice Chair Faber. Motion carried 4-1-0, with Chair Dunn, Vice Chair Faber, Councilor Paul, and Councilor Combes voting in favor, and Councilor Bouchard voting in opposition.
Vice Chair Faber moved to approve the consent agenda items as presented. Seconded by Councilor Combes. Motion carried 5-0-0. Chair votes in the affirmative.
He asked the Council to determine when they would like to discuss using UFB to offset the tax rate. The Council came to consensus that they would add that to the agenda for the November 16 meeting.

Londonderry Town Council Meeting Minutes
Monday, November 9, 2026 | 6:00 p.m.  
Moose Hill Council Chambers, Londonderry Town Hall 
Council Members Present: 
Chair Ron Dunn 
Vice Chair Shawn Faber 
Councilor Ted Combes 
Councilor Dan Bouchard 
Councilor Deb Paul 
Council Members Absent:

A. CALL TO ORDER
Cha
ir Dunn called the meeting to order at 6:00 p.m. and led the Pledge of Allegiance. 
B. PUBLIC COMMENT
Cha
ir Dunn opened public comment: 
Name: Richard Bielinski 
Address: 89 Hall Road 
Followed up on previous inquiries regarding the Fire Chief's compensation and contractual salary 
adjustments. Noted that Orange, Massachusetts hired a fire chief on October 14, inquiring why 
Londonderry officials were not informed, and urged the Council to stick to a default budget for the 
upcoming fiscal year to prevent tax increases. 
Name: Kristine Perez 
Address: 5 Wesley Drive 
Expressed frustration over the Town's failure to implement impact fees since collection ceased in 
February 2013, noting that significant commercial and residential growth in developments like
Londonderry Town Council Minutes — November 9, 2026 
Page 2 
Woodmont Commons, Technology Hill, and Brook Hollow has resulted in substantial lost revenue 
that could have supported projects like a new DPW facility. 
Name: Kevin Smith 
Address: 6 King Philip Drive 
Addressed the Council and Budget Committee regarding the upcoming FY 28 budget cycle, 
highlighting that school district tax growth has been slower than municipal tax growth over the 
past three years and recommending starting with the default budget to manage tax increases. 
Chair Dunn closed public comment. 
C. BOARD APPOINTMENTS & REAPPOINTMENTS 
1. Resignation of Meridel Allen from the Senior Resources Committee. 
The Council considered the resignation of Meridel Allen from the Senior Resources Committee. 
Councilor Bouchard moved that the Londonderry Town Council hereby accepts the resignation of Meridel 
Allen from the Senior Resources Committee. Seconded by Vice Chair Faber. Motion carried 5-0-0. Chair 
votes in the affirmative. 
D. PUBLIC HEARINGS 
None. 
E. NEW BUSINESS 
1. Budget Workshop 
Acting Town Manager Kim Bernard, Finance Director Justin Campo, and department heads 
presented the preliminary FY 28 department budget proposals and default budget comparisons: 
• Town Manager / Administration: Administrative Services Director Kirsten Hildonen and 
Acting Town Manager Kim Bernard presented the proposed Administration budget. The Town 
Manager department has a proposed budget of $547,623 (a decrease of $160,269 from FY27 
due to removing the Assistant Town Manager role). Discussion included potential future 
Assistant Town Manager staffing/stipend structures and establishing a college credit 
internship program ($12,000 concept). The other proposed Administration budgets are Town 
Council at $17,991, Budget Committee at $621, General Assistance at $149,250, Cultural 
Affairs at $48,130, Conservation at $3,500, and Legal Services at $420,000. The Councilors 
discussed the distribution of the General Assistance funds and how general assistance would 
best be administered. 
• Finance / Assessing: Finance Director Justin Campo and Assistant Assessor Laura Keeley 
presented the Finance and Assessing budgets. Finance proposed $40,995 over FY 27 ($150 
below default), highlighting ongoing ERP system replacement efforts. Assessing proposed a 
budget of $495,010 and reviewed property inspection requirements (20% annual cycle), sales
Londonderry Town Council Minutes — November 9, 2026 
Page 3 
visits, revaluation letters for the upcoming 2027 Town-wide revaluation, and commercial 
property assessment monitoring. 
• Building Department: Controller Sarah Jardim-Lee and building officials presented the 
Building Department budget of $546,013. Highlighted 2,869 permits issued and ongoing code 
enforcement inspections. Reviewed professional / technical services line ($45,000) for 
mosquito spraying and tick control, with Council requesting increased spraying at the Town 
Common during Concerts on the Common.
• Human Resources: HR Director Tara Koza and HR Administrator Cherie Fuller presented the 
HR proposed budget of $357,245 ($29,835 increase over FY 27, with $21,995 in default 
contractual wage/benefit increases and $7,840 in net operating increases). They presented 
detailed workforce growth data showing Londonderry's municipal workforce grew 23.7% over 
10 years (from 207 to 256 employees), clarified the tuition reimbursement ($21,500) supports 
all departments but lives in HR, recruitment advertising, wellness programs, and retiree 
support (50+ retirees).
• Information Technology: Cyber Services Director Jeremy Spaulding presented the IT proposed 
budget of $1,227,534 ($176,805 increase over FY 27; $120,548 above default). Highlighted 
management services software ($516,894), upcoming phone / internet contract expiration in 
March ($30,000 anticipated increase), hardware replacement ($91,700 for fire truck 
computers, ambulance modems, clerk displays), and expanding access control security system 
($40,000) to the Senior Center and Town Common.
• Planning & Economic Development: Director of Planning & Economic Development Jacob 
LaFontaine presented the proposed budget of $695,649 ($7,262 above default). Reviewed 
development review activities (85 applications annually generating approximately $45,000 in 
fee revenue), GIS management, master plan implementation, CIP coordination, and increased 
printing / notice costs driven by expanded 400-foot abutter notification requirements.
2. Receive a presentation from the Department of Public Works and Consultant Kimley
Horn regarding the Pavement Condition Index (PCI).
D
eputy Director of Public Works James Danis and Todd Connors from Kimley Horn presented the 
Pavement Condition Index (PCI) assessment report for Londonderry's 372.36 lane miles of 
roadways. Using automated van-mounted laser and camera technology, Kimley Horn evaluated all 
town-maintained streets on a 0 to 100 PCI scale. Londonderry achieved an overall average PCI 
score of 70 ('Good' condition), with extensive green (good) and yellow (mid-grade) road segments. 
The data will form the foundation for a five-year formalized road program and capital budget 
planning. 
3. Review and Consider Approval of the Tentative Collective Bargaining Agreement
with IAFF Local 3160, Subject to Voter Approval of the Cost Items.
A
cting Town Manager Kim Bernard and Finance Director Justin Campo presented Resolution 
2026-21 regarding the tentative successor collective bargaining agreement between the Town of 
Londonderry and IAFF Local 3160 for the period July 1, 2027 through June 30, 2030, ratified by 
union membership on October 15, 2026. Key substantive changes include: updating wage scales
Londonderry Town Council Minutes — November 9, 2026 
Page 4 
(for FY 28 to FY 30); health insurance town HDHP contributions of 100% (FY 28), 95% (FY 29), 
and 90% (FY 30) with increased HSA contributions ($1,000 single / $2,000 family) and dependent 
care FSA match up to $2,500; health insurance buyout alignment ($12,000 family); disciplinary 
authority clarification putting suspensions / demotion s/ terminations under Town Manager 
authority; grievance procedure updates for demotion / suspension/termination starting at Step 
Two; military leave alignment with Town Policy ADM-132; and educational incentive pay 
increases. 
Councilor Bouchard moved that the Londonderry Town Council hereby approve the tentative successor 
collective bargaining agreement between the Town and IAFF Local 3160 for July 1, 2027 through June 
30, 2030, subject to voter approval of applicable cost items and other required approvals. Seconded by 
Councilor Combes. Motion carried 5-0-0. Chair votes in the affirmative. 
4. Discuss & schedule a public hearing on the proposed Water Special Assessment 
District 
Administrative Services Director Kirsten Hildonen presented the proposed Water Special 
Assessment District under RSA 52-A and RSA 162-X to assist homeowners with connecting to 
newly constructed water mains. The district covers approximately 179 eligible residential 
properties along High Range Road, Parmenter Road, Old Nashua Road, and South Road, utilizing 
$400,000 appropriated from Undesignated Fund Balance at the March 2026 Town Election. 
Participation is voluntary, offering 100% net cost financing ($2,000 minimum to $30,000 cap) 
repaid over 2 to 15 years via semiannual tax bills with zero interest. 
Vice Chair Faber moved that the Londonderry Town Council hereby schedules a public hearing on 
November 30, 2026 at 7 p.m. in the Moose Hill Chambers of the Londonderry Town Hall on the 
proposed Water Special Assessment District. Seconded by Councilor Paul. Motion carried 5-0-0. Chair 
votes in the affirmative. 
F. OLD BUSINESS 
1. Discuss and authorize the Town Manager to execute the Off-Site Improvement 
Agreement with PE Realty Partners (Procopio). 
Administrative Services Director Kirsten Hildonen and Acting Town Manager Kim Bernard 
presented the Off-Site Improvement Agreement for Procopio's Thornton Hill (250 cottage-court 
homes at 36 Pillsbury Road) and Rosecrans Drive (60 units at 44 Pillsbury Road) developments 
within Woodmont Commons, continued from November 2. Procopio will construct a left-turn lane 
on Pillsbury Road into Thornton Hill (plans due Dec 1, 2026; work starts Apr 15, 2027; substantial 
completion Nov 15, 2027) and three-way stop improvements at Pillsbury / Michels Way. In lieu of 
constructing a right-turn lane at Pillsbury / Gilcreast, Procopio will convey land easements valued 
at $345,600 (at 15, 36, and 44 Pillsbury Road) and pay a net final cash payment of $130,546.25 
(plus up to $5,250 for Hardy/Pillsbury signage) prior to the first building permit. Up to 25 
certificates of occupancy may issue prior to substantial completion of the left-turn lane, subject to 
Planning Board amendment of the Notices of Decision on December 2, 2026. Director of Planning
Londonderry Town Council Minutes — November 9, 2026 
Page 5 
and Economic Development Jacob LaFontaine and Attorney Laura Gandia from Devine Millimet 
(representing Procopio) were also in attendance to answer questions. 
Councilor Combes moved that the Londonderry Town Council hereby authorizes the Acting Town 
Manager to enter into the Off-Site Improvements Agreement and to take all actions necessary to 
effectuate the agreement. Seconded by Vice Chair Faber. Motion carried 4-1-0, with Chair Dunn, Vice 
Chair Faber, Councilor Paul, and Councilor Combes voting in favor, and Councilor Bouchard voting in 
opposition. 
G. APPROVAL OF CONSENT ITEMS 
1. 2026-11-02 Sewer Warrant 
Vice Chair Faber moved to approve the consent agenda items as presented. Seconded by Councilor 
Combes. Motion carried 5-0-0. Chair votes in the affirmative. 
H. OTHER BUSINESS 
1. Liaison Reports 
Councilor Deb Paul reported on attending the annual Veterans Breakfast, highlighting strong 
community turnout, recognizing the oldest attending veteran (102 years old), and commending 
guest speaker Bo Butler for an inspiring presentation. 
2. Town Manager Report 
Finance Director Justin Campo provided an update regarding NHDRA property tax rate setting, 
noting all portal filings were approved and tax rate setting figures were expected shortly. He 
asked the Council to determine when they would like to discuss using UFB to offset the tax rate. 
The Council came to consensus that they would add that to the agenda for the November 16 
meeting. 
I. PUBLIC COMMENT 
Chair Dunn opened public comment: 
Name: Tony DiFrancesco 
Address: 11 Chester Court 
Expressed concern over Councilor Bouchard’s comments questioning the reliability of municipal 
bonding, asserting that town bonding has proven reliable throughout Londonderry's history, and 
stated that assessing a property is different than a real estate agent’s view on its value. 
Chair Dunn closed public comment. 
Councilor Bouchard raised concerns regarding a legal billing invoice totaling over $125,000 from 
outside counsel (Attorney Christopher Vrountas) that contained $29,935 in line items with 
redactions, arguing that Council members should review unredacted invoices. Councilor Paul 
concurred that the Council should inspect detailed billing entries. Vice Chair Shawn Faber and
Londonderry Town Council Minutes — November 9, 2026 
Page 6 
Chair Dunn clarified that redactions protect attorney-client privilege regarding ongoing litigation 
and warned against disclosing privileged executive strategy in public session. 
Chair Dunn closed public comment. 
J. NON-PUBLIC SESSION 
None held. 
K. ADJOURNMENT
Vice Chair Faber moved to adjourn the meeting. Seconded by Councilor Combes. Motion carried 5-0-0.
Chair votes in the affirmative. The meeting adjourned at 10:06 p.m.
